Tab 1 · Connect

Tell the app where the agent lives

You enter

Google Cloud project, location and app ID, then click Connect.

It shows

Every agent in that app in a dropdown, and the chosen agent’s current instructions.

If it fails

A red message says why: wrong app ID, no access, or not signed in to Google Cloud.

Real connection to the demo agent in project enrichment-conv-sf, location us. The app remembers the last project and app ID in your browser.

Tab 2 · Scenarios

Write the test calls in plain English

Save checks the file first and explains any mistake, such as a missing goal or a repeated ID.

FieldWhat it controls
personaHow the caller talks and behaves
goalWhat the caller wants
factsWhat the caller knows if asked
success_criteriaWhat counts as a pass
policiesRules checked on every call
splittrain = practice, holdout = exam
max_turnsCaller turns before cut-off
voice, noiseAccent, speed, background (audio)

The real suite used for the live runs. Replace the six sample calls with your own, or let the AI generator above the editor draft them from a PRD.

Tab 3 · Evaluate

Four settings, then Run evaluation

Trials

How many times each test call runs. Use 2–3 to smooth out lucky or unlucky calls.

Mode

Text turns run in seconds. Full audio speaks every line, like a real call.

Background noise

Audio only. One noise for every call, or each call’s own setting.

Use tool fakes

On by default. The bot’s order and account lookups use pretend data.

Real run shown: text mode, tool fakes off because the demo agent’s tools already hold test data. Only one run can happen at a time.

Tab 3 · Evaluate results

The report card, then one row per call

Train / holdout reward: overall score 0–1 on practice and exam calls

Task success: calls where the caller got what they needed

Policy adherence: house rules followed

Groundedness: nothing made up

Voice-clean turns: bot turns with no phone-quality flag

Response gap: silence before the bot answers, typical and worst

ASR word error: how much of the caller the bot misheard

Orange tags count each phone-quality problem across all calls

Click any row to open that call

Real run on the demo agent before coaching: 5 of 6 calls passed, rules followed in half of them, 16 replies too long to speak.

Pop-up · One call

Replay a call and see why it scored that way

Title line

Which test call, its score, and how it ended: caller hung up, bot ended it, or turn limit.

Left: the conversation

Grey bubbles are the caller, white are the bot. Each has a play button. Bot turns show the silence before answering and how long it spoke.

“Agent heard”

Appears when the bot misheard, with the share of words it got wrong.

Right: the scorer

A summary, sub-scores, and each problem tied to the turn number where it happened.

Real call (text mode, so no audio players): the scorer caught the agent reading out m.ortiz@example.com at turn 7.

Tab 4 · Auto-improve

Same settings, plus rounds and a safety tick-box

Iterations

How many coaching rounds to try. Each round re-runs every test call, so audio rounds take a while.

Sandbox tick-box

Required. Confirms this is a copy of the bot, because trial instructions are written to it during the run.

Start loop

Saves the original instructions, runs a baseline, then coaches. The original goes back at the end.

Real run on the demo agent: 1 coaching round, text mode. Trials, mode, noise and tool fakes work exactly as on the Evaluate tab.

Tab 4 · Auto-improve results

A chart of each round and a verdict on every change

Chart: solid blue is practice calls, dashed grey is exam calls. A dot means kept, a cross means rejected.

OutcomeMeaning
baselineThe bot as it is today
keptBetter on practice, no worse on exam
rejectedNo real gain, or exam calls got worse
invalidRemoved a tool or structure; never tested

Each row: the coach’s diagnosis and changes, plus Diff, Episodes and Apply.

Real run: practice 0.58 → 0.80, exam 0.78 → 0.85, so round 1 was kept. Rejected and invalid rounds look the same, marked in the Outcome column.

Pop-up · Diff, then Apply

Read the change, then decide

1 · Review

Green is added, red is removed. Here the coach added email masking, read-back and a voice-clarity rule.

2 · Apply

Asks for confirmation, then writes that version to the bot copy.

Changed your mind?

Restore original instruction puts the old version back at any time.

Real Diff from the coaching run on the demo agent. Apply appears only after a run finishes, and only for the app the run used.

Tab 5 · History

Every run is kept and can be reopened

What’s listed

Newest first: when it ran, Evaluate or Auto-improve, text or audio, which agent, and status.

Click a row

Opens its results tab exactly as it finished, recordings included. A running job shows live progress.

Where it’s saved

On disk, or in a Cloud Storage bucket when deployed on Google Cloud, so it survives restarts.

Real runs on the demo agent, with a coaching run in progress, above the earlier demo-data runs. Run IDs are the start date and time.

Putting it together

A first session, in order

1

Connect to a copy of the bot, never the live one

5

Auto-improve: 2 rounds, 2 trials, sandbox ticked

2

Scenarios: swap the samples for 10–20 of your real call reasons

6

Diff the kept round with the business owner, then Apply

3

Evaluate in text, 1 trial. Open 3–4 calls and check you agree with the scorer

7

Evaluate again to confirm, then release through the normal process

4

Evaluate in full audio to check listening and speaking
